title: The Timetable, Not the Phone
story: When the station clock and her phone disagreed, Ruth trusted the printed timetable and stayed on the platform. The train arrived by the clock, and the guard confirmed that the timetable still governed departures. Her phone had kept the time zone of the city she had left. She corrected it before the next connection. An ignored mismatch would have sent her onward an hour early.

vocabulary.definition: The printed list of departure times
A difference between two things that should agree
A later train she still needed to catch

quiz.question: What did Ruth trust when the clock and the phone disagreed?
options: The printed timetable
The time showing on her phone
The city she had just left
A clock inside the arriving train
quiz.explanation: She trusted the printed timetable and stayed on the platform.
quiz.supportingSentence: When the station clock and her phone disagreed, Ruth trusted the printed timetable and stayed on the platform.

quiz.question: Why was the phone showing the wrong time?
options: It still used the time zone of the city she had left
The guard had reset it during the journey
The station clock was running an hour fast
The timetable had been printed in another country
quiz.correctAnswer: It still used the time zone of the city she had left
quiz.explanation: The phone had kept the time zone of the city she had left.
quiz.supportingSentence: Her phone had kept the time zone of the city she had left.

quiz.question: What would following the phone have done?
options: It would have sent her on an hour too soon
It would have cancelled the next connection
It would have put her on a train going back
It would have hidden the printed timetable
quiz.correctAnswer: It would have sent her on an hour too soon
quiz.explanation: Ignoring the mismatch would have sent her onward an hour early.
quiz.supportingSentence: An ignored mismatch would have sent her onward an hour early.

quiz.question: What does governed mean about the timetable?
options: It decided which departure times were official
It was painted on the station wall
It had been cancelled after the disagreement
It was folded into the margin of a ticket
quiz.correctAnswer: It decided which departure times were official
quiz.explanation: The guard said the timetable still governed departures, so it set the official leaving times.
quiz.supportingSentence: The train arrived by the clock, and the guard confirmed that the timetable still governed departures.

quiz.question: Why does the writer end with the mismatch that was avoided?
options: To show what trusting the wrong time would have cost
To prove the guard rewrote the timetable
To suggest Ruth preferred travelling after dark
To argue that phones should replace station clocks
quiz.correctAnswer: To show what trusting the wrong time would have cost
quiz.explanation: The last sentence states the early departure she would have made if she had ignored the difference.
quiz.supportingSentence: An ignored mismatch would have sent her onward an hour early.
